Hi everyone!

For many, the start of the year is a time for setting goals and planning for the future. This is something we have been focused on here at BioWare Austin. 2014 was an amazing year for the team. We delivered two expansions, an overhaul to the class system, and regular story updates through Flashpoints. I’m proud of what the team has accomplished, and we would not have been able to do it without your support – thank you. I’m excited for what we have in store for you in 2015.

Some of you might remember before launch, we talked a lot about the “four pillars” of RPGs – combat, exploration, progression and story. Star Wars™: The Old Republic™ is an MMO, but it’s also a BioWare game. Three years ago, we set out to deliver a product that contained the best of two worlds – the immersive story experience from a single-player RPG and the vast array of systems and social connection from an online multiplayer game. Since launch, we have mainly focused on the latter, adding Galactic Strongholds, achievements, legacy perks, reputation tracks, and Galactic Starfighter. But with the success of the Shadow of Revan expansion, we think it’s time that we return to our roots and what truly makes our game unique: story.

Shadow of Revan was just the beginning. In 2015, we are committed to bringing you more character-driven adventures in the Old Republic universe. You’re going to see a unified story, with a focus on themes that unite our eight classes – everyone is a veteran from the Galactic Civil War with a complicated past and an uncertain future. You’ll see a greater emphasis on your character’s personal history, and on the choices you make. I don’t want to say too much more since we are still in the midst of development, but what we have planned really gets back to the Star Wars™ fantasy at the heart of our game.

Our plan is to deliver two major updates with this new story direction later this year – one in the summer and the other by the end of the year. But what’s happening in the meantime, you ask? Below is a list of some of what you can expect in the first half of the year. As always, please keep in mind that all of this is subject to change. We reserve the right to adjust our plans if we feel it is necessary.

February 12th: Game Update 3.1 Hard Mode Flashpoint: Blood Hunt Hard Mode Flashpoint: Battle for Rishi Start of PvP Season 4 Spring: Game Update 3.2 Outfit Designer Stay tuned for a blog on this awesome new feature coming soon! A new story arc on the planet Ziost. This story arc takes us to the Imperial homeworld of Ziost, where we answer many of the questions posed by the cliffhanger at the end of Shadow of Revan. End of PvP Season 4 and the Start of Season 5 And Beyond! New Stronghold Playable Togruta – I kind of let the Cathar out of the bag on this one last year at the New York Cantina, but now it’s in writing! There’s still more to be revealed for Star Wars: The Old Republic this year – this is just the start! When we are further along in development, we will post more information that dive into the nitty-gritty details for these new features.

I want to thank you, our galactic heroes, for continuing to support us. It’s your feedback and enthusiasm that makes Star Wars: The Old Republic a better game and drives us to be better. All of our hard work is for you.

May the Force™ be With You!

Bruce Maclean Senior Producer

n February, we celebrate Valentine's Day. To be exact, February 14 is the day associated with deep friendship and romantic love in many countries around the world. On that day, some see it as a tradition for lovers or for good friends to express their feelings for each other by presenting flowers, offering confectionery, or simply by sending greeting cards, for instance.

Also in Tibia it is possible to celebrate Valentine's Day, and to send a special gift to your loved one. Since 2008, NPC Valentina has been appearing in Greenshore on that day to sell Valentine items like cards, heart cakes, flower bouquets and presents. Since 2010, she is also offering the much loved heart backpacks, however, her stock is limited so you can only buy one each year.

By the way, we community managers have a real life heart backpack hanging on our office wall. We received this hand-made gift from the Henceforth Family in 2011.

If the rumours around the Tibian world are true, Valentina will offer a couple of new love-goods this year. A poem was found that was - allegedly - written by her. It obviously contains some advertising ideas for her valentine business:

Words to express your love are sometimes hard to find words to describe this feeling often don't come to your mind. A ring could help you symbolise quite clearly how you feel, however, the seriousness it conveys might not really be an appeal.

Flowers then are a lighter choice, they might help you find your inner voice. Given as single, combined to a few, or as a bouquet, the only problem: they tend to fade away.

Nevertheless, roses are a wonderful gift, however, they still have a very romantic drift. If both choices are way too daring for you, something cuter might be the clue.

What about a sweet teddy, hugging a heart. Some women will find this a wonderful piece of art. They will understand what you are trying to say, and will be reminded of you even when you're away.

As usual, Valentine will only be there for Valentine's day. So if you are desperately in need for a gift for your beloved one, or simply curious to see whether the rumours are true, you really need to keep this date in mind and cannot be late.

This day is not only about expressing your love for somebody, though. It is about love and harmony in general, about connections to people around the world. Since Tibia is the most obvious thing that connects all of us, community members and CipSoft members, we have asked around in the office what people love about Tibia. Several colleagues have answered this question, and we would like to share the responses with you. At the same time, we want to invite you to share with us what you love about Tibia, too.

Here is what some of our colleagues stated:

Lyxoph (Graphic Artist): I love the excitement of fighting a strong monster I've never fought before for the first time. I love that after so many years, I still keep discovering new mysterious places in the world. And I love how this microcosm is kept alive through all the players inhabiting it, the legends they built and the adventures they experienced.

Evonary (Game Designer): I deeply love Tibia's very unique style - games of this kind are rare nowadays. In this huge gameworld I can choose what I do, but anything comes with a possible consequence, for example how I possibly risk my very own death in every corner I explore. Everytime I play the game it's a different experience and every time I log in I can choose something different to do. Oh and of course I really love some good self-made Tibian cookies <3

Cedeko (Programmer): The many surprises that could be laying in wait in just about every unexplored nook and corner of Tibia's world. Whenever I venture out of town, I could come upon a beautiful land formation, a species of monsters I've never seen before, or even just a book telling obscure details about Tibia's past. Few games these days have this sort of depth when it comes to free exploration.

Tjured (Community Manager): I love Tibia because it offers you an almost endless variety how to spend your time. You can either work on your level progress, explore the unknown, do quests, fight other players, or just chat with others and thereby get in touch with people from all over the world. In short you can kill, die, flee, cry, laugh, win, lose, talk, run, stand, and maybe someday, even sit. :)

Teyrata (Game Content Designer): I love the sense of adventure in Tibia: the wide world to explore, full of jungles, deserts, plains and mountains; the thrill of not exactly knowing if behind the next corner there is a fight, a monster, or something unexpected happening - I always step out being on my guard and ready for adventure. Bring it on!

Rejana (Community Manager): I love the possibilities Tibia offers to be creative. There is so much freedom to do whatever you want besides levelling: decorating houses, buidling things like "parcel castles", outlining a soccerfield with gold coins to play in, role play, etc. There are just so many ways to have fun. And even though I've never reached very high levels, I also really appreciate the fact that there is no end. No matter how long it takes, you will grow stronger and bigger with every hunt you go on.

Lionet (Game Content Designer): I like Tibia because it offers me a considerable amount of freedom as a player. Especially the sandbox elements of the world are what I am always looking for in an RPG in general. I also like that it doesn't hold your hand at every step while still containing a large amount of quests and story experiences. It's a very difficult game at times but you always feel you really achieved something when you reach the end of a quest, kill a boss or find valuable treasure. The worth of items, the sense of achievement and feeling of accomplishment is often a weakness in modern games, so for me Tibia is one of the few remaining safe havens in terms of old school gameplay and content.

So - what about you? What do you love about Tibia?

Happy Valentine's Day! Your Community Managers
